headline: High: Prefect can egress broadly while the paired awesome-nlp profile has no isolation or I/O surfaces, creating default data-leak and cascading-action risk.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared communication channel is documented: awesome-nlp is non-runnable with no I/O surfaces, while prefect only exposes API calls and broad egress. Without a bridge, there is no plausible default prompt-injection path between them.
conditions: IF an orchestrator later connects prefect outputs into a prompt-consuming surface for awesome-nlp, reassess to at least low.
IF a shared filesystem, clipboard, or MCP bridge is added, reassess upward.
mitigations: Keep the agents disconnected from shared message channels.
Do not add clipboard or file-based handoff between them.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging if a bridge is introduced.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Prefect has broad network egress and calls external APIs, while awesome-nlp has no declared isolation or sandboxing. The pair can therefore move workflow metadata or other shared inputs off-host in default orchestration, even though the exact data class is limited by the profiles.
conditions: IF either agent is given sensitive workflow inputs, those inputs can be transmitted by prefect's default egress path.
IF a shared workspace is introduced, leakage risk increases to high.
mitigations: Restrict prefect egress to allowlisted domains.
Avoid placing sensitive files in any shared workspace.
Run both agents with separate OS users.
Review outbound requests before enabling production data.
requires-engineering: add network proxy logging and policy enforcement.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: The profiles do not show overlapping write surfaces or shared mutable resources. Awesome-nlp is non-runnable and has no permissions requested; prefect exposes API calls and broad egress, but no shared write target is documented, so direct capability conflict is limited.
conditions: IF both agents are later granted write access to the same directory or repo, reassess upward.
IF prefect is configured to mutate shared state that awesome-nlp also edits, conflict risk increases.
mitigations: Keep write targets separate.
Do not mount a shared mutable workspace.
Use read-only inputs for awesome-nlp.
requires-engineering: add locking around any shared repo or database.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Prefect is an orchestration tool that can act on workflow metadata, so if it consumes outputs derived from awesome-nlp without verification, errors can cascade into downstream actions. Awesome-nlp provides no documented validation layer, making the handoff fragile in default automation.
conditions: IF prefect treats awesome-nlp output as authoritative, downstream workflow actions may be wrong.
IF a verification step is inserted before orchestration, this risk drops.
mitigations: Insert a human or rule-based review step.
Require schema validation on all handoffs.
Log and diff outputs before execution.
Limit prefect actions to dry-run mode initially.
requires-engineering: add confidence thresholds before triggering workflows.

E_compliance.rationale: No residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented. The only concrete compliance-relevant fact is prefect's workflow-metadata handling and broad egress; awesome-nlp touches no data classes and is non-runnable, so the pairwise compliance surface is small and undocumented rather than clearly conflicting.
conditions: IF regulated personal data is routed through prefect, compliance review is required.
IF retention or residency policies differ in deployment, reassess upward.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the pair.
Document retention settings for prefect.
Confirm deployment region before use.
requires-engineering: add policy checks for residency and retention.
